claims.text: Toughness retention in CoCrFeMnNi is governed by an optimal stacking-fault energy that balances dislocation slip and deformation twinning.
Adding 5 at% Al to CoCrFeMnNi lowers its stacking-fault energy.
Lowering stacking-fault energy through Al addition promotes deformation twinning.
Increased deformation twinning enhances work hardening.
Increased deformation twinning impedes crack propagation.
Changing stacking-fault energy beyond an optimal range causes premature strain localization and toughness loss.
The baseline CoCrFeMnNi alloy has higher stacking-fault energy than the proposed Al-modified alloy.
The baseline CoCrFeMnNi alloy exhibits lower twinning activity than the proposed Al-modified alloy.
A moderate reduction in stacking-fault energy increases the propensity for deformation twinning.
Interactions between deformation twins and dislocation slip increase work-hardening capacity.
Interactions between deformation twins and dislocation slip increase energy dissipation during deformation.
The increased work hardening and energy dissipation produced by twinning allow the alloy to retain higher toughness.
Reducing stacking-fault energy too far can cause excessive twinning or localized deformation and thereby embrittle the alloy.
The 5 at% Al-modified alloy will have greater fracture toughness than the baseline alloy.
The Al-modified alloy will exhibit greater work hardening than the baseline alloy.
The Al-modified alloy will show delayed crack initiation under intermediate strain rates relative to the baseline.
The baseline alloy has lower resistance to crack propagation than the proposed Al-modified alloy.
The proposed behavior may cease to apply at temperatures or strain rates that activate diffusion-driven processes or phase transformations.
